<reason>Side B (PRO) won a clear but competitive debate. A's strongest weapon was the "fork": strict limits either require age verification for all adults or collapse into a mere toggle. B dissolved this with the defaults framework — protections bind from install regardless of any age flag, and only adults who opt out verify identity, mirrored on alcohol/gambling age-gating. A's late counter (every adult buying a skin must "volunteer" ID to every publisher, fragmenting verification across countless gem shops) was a real hit B never fully answered, but B's weighing — minor adult friction versus systematic childhood exposure — stayed cleaner. B also exposed a genuine coverage gap A never closed: the child who types "18" on their own account with a linked card is protected by B's install-time defaults but missed by A's opt-in platform locks; A's symmetry argument only covered the parent-account-sharing child. B answered pressure questions directly and honestly (conceding the age flag is defeatable while showing the case never depended on it), and B's layered-regulation answer (seatbelts and speed limits) absorbed A's clever toll-collector reversal. A's rebuttals were sharp and rhetorically excellent, and both sides suffered one clipped turn, but A's case progressively conceded harm while relocating the fix, and B's closing crystallized the decisive comparison better.</best_rebuttal>The decisive exchange was B's Rebuttal 2 (B4.3–B4.4) dissolving A's verification fork: conceding the age flag is defeatable but showing that defaults — per-purchase confirmation, no stored payment, caps from install — bind lying and honest children identically, with only opting-out adults bearing verification. A's Rebuttal 2 counter (B4.4 means every adult verifies to every publisher, the fork "embraced in their own words") landed hard but was blunted by B's alcohol/gambling opt-out analogy and never addressed B's coverage of the typed-18 child on a fresh account.</best_rebuttal>
